question: In a logic circuit, three SPST (Single Pole Single Throw) switches are used to implement a logic gate. The switches are connected in series. What will be the output of the circuit if all the switches are closed?

options.text: The output will depend on the type of gate used

solution:
The correct answer is __1**(The output will be 1)**.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• SPST switches__ are simple on/off devices.
 
• When three SPST switches are connected in series, the circuit will only be complete if __all switches are closed__.
 
• In logic terms, this configuration implements an AND gate.
 
• If all switches are closed (ON), the circuit is complete, and the output will be logic 1.
 
• For any switch open (OFF), the circuit is broken, and the output will be logic 0.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Logic Gates:**

 
 
• Logic gates are the basic building blocks of digital circuits.
 
• They perform basic logic functions such as AND, OR, and NOT.
 
 
 
• **SPST Switches:**
 
 
• SPST stands for Single Pole Single Throw.
 
• It is one of the most basic types of switches, acting as an on/off toggle.
 
 
 
• **Series Configuration:**
 
 
• In a series configuration, the current must pass through all components sequentially.
 
• The circuit is incomplete if any one component is disconnected.
